evidence.detail: Exact v308 rs/g/a stores exactly four mutable ints and has constructors (x,y,width,height) plus (width,height), where the two-arg form delegates to (0,0,width,height); its two mutators set the low/origin pair and high/size pair respectively.

The base client rs/C returns rs/g/a from its container-bounds method, constructs it from the live container width/height after subtracting frame insets, and reads the high/size pair to update the active client width/height.

Public RuneLite/OSRS client lineage exposes the structurally identical utility as Bounds with lowX, lowY, highX, highY, setLow, setHigh, the same two constructors and the same null toString implementation.

candidates.note: Bounds is fixed by exact-v308 structure/client use and a field-for-field inherited RuneLite/OSRS lineage match.
